I think if we're honest, We all have a little bit of Pharisee in us that, that says to be Christian is to have faith in Jesus and to be a lot like me, to dress like me and to think like me and to read like me and to vote like me.

lines.text: This is where the process of rebuilding ruined lives begins, with right worship, and in particular, with atonement for sin.
Where do you even begin when the world is a wreck, when your life is a mess? The message of Ezra 3 is simple. Worship is where it all begins.
Worship never stays in the heart. Worship comes out our fingertips in the real world.
It's one thing to talk lofty words about God, to have lots of devotional thoughts, to feel all the right feelings, but that should translate into action.
Whenever your life is a mess, big or small, start at the cross. Start with repentance and faith.

Ezra-Nehemiah reveals the way that God works so that you can be renewed in your life today through faith in Jesus Christ as weak and finite and sinful creatures, we are desperately in need of revival.

lines.text: In every instance of salvation, at the beginning of the process that results in a heart that's transformed by God, there must first take place a confrontation. A confrontation between the Almighty One and the rebellious creature, between the author of life and a person who is dead in their trespasses.

Jesus is sovereignly advancing his kingdom by seeking out those whom the Father has given him. He's confronting them with his glory. He's transforming their hearts by his grace, and he's bringing them into his flock regardless of their background, their past or present condition, so that they might belong to him and him alone and be commissioned for his purposes.

Jesus has not only saved us from something, but he has saved us to something. Namely, he has saved us to be his witnesses on this earth, to bear his name, to take his message to the world, a world that is lost and a world that has no hope of saving itself.

No, Scripture here is telling us that God acts in the exact opposite manner. Here on these pages, we're reading about a God who is proactive. Seeking the lost, a God who willingly places himself before us and he bids us to come toward his loving-kindness.

No one has been saved like this, and yet the truth is every single one of God's people have been saved just like this. Because Jesus has taken the same actions to save each life. He has performed the same miraculous work of his marvelous, marvelous grace in your heart if indeed you are in him today.

Jesus, who is building his kingdom by transforming the hearts of his people, brings about the salvation of his people first by confronting his people. And for Saul on the Damascus Road, this confrontation is one-sided. For as impressive as a persecutor of the church he had been, he is completely overpowered in this moment.

lines.text: The Spirit of God invites us to the privilege of work. Our passage reveals the joy of working, knowing that God is the only one doing the work, and that already ought to set our expectations to wonder, what is the joy of work?

Work becomes a privilege when we see God do what only God can do. While the passage teaches us to remember who really does the work, it also invites us to go to work, all along knowing we get to go to work and watch as the master crafts what we could never.

The privilege of work is that our vocation is shaped, our vocation is shaped not just by craft, but by the wonder and the amazement of working alongside the Creator. It is work because it does require real engagement and ownership, but it is a privilege because no other seat brings you as close to the splendor of seeing God work and protect.

The most apparent is that while every task the Lord gives us requires action on our part, he ultimately does what is needed. This both reveals our responsibility and our dependence. He calls us to trust and to act simultaneously.
The privilege of enjoyment overflows when paired with work and seeing God work.

You see, we can think of a lot of things that we want to see the Lord build. But the interesting thing is, is that the family that the Lord would build in the line of David would have one purpose, and it was not so that the line of David would be great. It would be so the world would get its Savior.
